text:
maria.dev: Hey — running into weird behavior in the Go SDK when cancelling streaming generator calls from a sample app. Context cancel sometimes leaves goroutines around and other times the generator keeps emitting a final chunk after ctx is cancelled.

alex.m: ugh. can you paste the minimal sample?

maria.dev: here's the stripped-down flow:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
defer cancel()
stream, err := client.Generator().Stream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { return err }
for {
    chunk, err := stream.Recv()
    if err == io.EOF { break }
    if err != nil { return err }
    fmt.Println(chunk.Text)
}
```
Sometimes when the timeout hits the loop returns with an error, sometimes it prints one more chunk and then hangs. On our dev machines it leaks ~2 goroutines (observed with pprof).

samir.k: that code looks right. Are you using token refresh middleware? we had a similar symptom where mid-stream the auth refresh triggered a retry and the runtime appended a retried tail token, so user sees duplicates and the stream state goes weird.

maria.dev: yes we're using automatic refresh with the default http client. The weird part is cancellation - sometimes the client-side context cancel doesn't propagate to the underlying runtime until the next token refresh or write.

alex.m: I'm guessing two separate issues: 1) stream cancellation propagation (should stop background send/recv ASAP), 2) auth retry can cause mid-stream restart which the generator doesn't surface as a distinct error. We should make the semantics explicit: ctx cancellation => immediate stream.CloseWithError(context.Canceled) or similar.

jenni.ops: +1 on explicit CloseWithError. From an onboarding perspective this bites users — our sample app uses context timeout for user abort and people hit leaks. Can we add a tiny sample that shows correct cancellation pattern and add to quickstarts?

maria.dev: I prototyped a small change in the sample app where we wrap Recv with select on ctx.Done:
```go
for {
  select {
  case <-ctx.Done():
    _ = stream.Close() // best-effort close to unblock runtime
    return ctx.Err()
  default:
  }
  chunk, err := stream.Recv()
  ...
}
```
That reduces leaks but doesn't fix the times when Recv unblocks after Close and returns a nil chunk.

samir.k: the SDK should guarantee Recv returns non-nil chunk only if no error. if Close() can race, we should expose CloseWithError so the runtime can surface a context.Canceled explicitly.

alex.m: also callout — when HTTP 401/refresh happens mid-stream we currently do an automatic retry which can produce duplicate end-fragments. We probably need a retry policy: retries allowed for unary calls but streaming generator retries should be a no-op or escalate to an explicit error explaining partial output. Document this too.

jenni.ops: For DX: add a one-line note in quickstart: "Do not rely on automatic generator retries for streaming calls; handle ctx cancellations by calling stream.CloseWithError and treat partial output as incomplete." Link to a sample snippet.

maria.dev: filing a small RFC in repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/??? (WIP) — proposes:
- add Stream.CloseWithError(err error)
- ensure Recv never returns a non-nil chunk with a non-nil error
- disable automatic auth retries for open streaming connections; surface a clear 401 mid-stream error
- add sample app showing recommended cancellation pattern + test that checks no goroutine leaks

ci-bot: CI: tests/streaming-cancelation-test triggered by comment by maria.dev — running golang race+pprof job :white_check_mark:

samir.k: If people agree I can implement the CloseWithError and a small integration test in the runtime binding. Also will add an explicit note in SDK docs about auth refresh behavior for streams.

alex.m: agreed. small UX ask: make the CloseWithError call idempotent and safe to call from signal handlers.

jenni.ops: Can we add a short troubleshooting blurb in the console docs too so users see the "why did my generator keep running" pattern? People often search docs first.

maria.dev: thanks all — I'll push the sample app change and link the PR here when ready. For now pinning the sample in quickstarts to avoid confusing new users. :sparkles:
